behaviour: After a direct entity lookup misses, attempts former-ref resolution once and redirects to the renamed entity's URL preserving the sub-path, query and fragment, carrying the former ref in navigation state.
rules: 1. This hook is the SINGLE shared seam: both frontend systems import it (legacy components/CatalogEntityPage/CatalogEntityPage.tsx and alpha alpha/components/CatalogEntityPage.tsx), so one implementation serves both. Do not move this logic into a component — a component reaches only one system.

2. Keep the existing `useAsyncRetry` direct lookup exactly as it is, and keep the hook's return type `EntityLoadingStatus` and its four returned fields unchanged. A URL that resolves normally must issue NO additional request: every new step below is gated on `entity` being undefined after loading finished.

3. Add a `useRef<string | null>(null)` named `attemptedRefRef`, holding the stringified ref the hook has already attempted resolution for. Compute the current requested ref once with `stringifyEntityRef({ kind, namespace, name })`. This mirrors the `checkedEntityRef` guard in plugins/techdocs useExternalRedirect and prevents a duplicate attempt across the remounts a replace-navigation causes.

4. Add a second `useAsync` (not useAsyncRetry) whose body returns `undefined` immediately unless ALL of: `name` is set, `loading` is false, `error` is undefined, `entity` is undefined, and `attemptedRefRef.current !== requestedRef`. Otherwise it sets `attemptedRefRef.current = requestedRef` and returns `await resolveFormerEntityRef(catalogApi, requestedRef)`. Its dependency array is `[catalogApi, requestedRef, entity, loading, error]`.

5. In a `useEffect` watching that second async's value: when the value's status is 'resolved', compute the target URL and call `navigate(target, { replace: true, state: { formerEntityRef: value.formerEntityRef } })`. When the status is 'unknown' or the value is undefined, do nothing at all — no navigate, no state, so the existing not-found UI renders unchanged.

6. TARGET URL CONSTRUCTION, preserving the sub-path: get `entityRoute = useRouteRef(entityRouteRef)`; compute `oldBase = entityRoute({ kind, namespace, name })` and `newBase = entityRoute(entityRouteParams(value.entity))`. Take `location.pathname` from `useLocation()`; if it starts with `oldBase`, the target pathname is `newBase` followed by the remainder after `oldBase`; otherwise fall back to `newBase` alone. Append `location.search` and `location.hash` verbatim. This is what makes /catalog/default/component/old-name/docs land on /catalog/default/component/new-name/docs. Import entityRouteParams and entityRouteRef from '@backstage/plugin-catalog-react'.
7. NO REDIRECT LOOP: the destination's direct lookup succeeds, so the gate in rule 4 is false there and resolution is never entered again for it. Do not add a counter or a URL parameter.
8. Carry the former ref ONLY in navigation state, never as a query parameter — the URL the user may re-share must stay clean, and the notice must not reappear on a direct reload.
9. Leave the existing `useEffect` that posts an error and navigates to '/' when `name` is missing exactly as it is.

10. Import resolveFormerEntityRef from '@backstage/catalog-client' and stringifyEntityRef from '@backstage/catalog-model'; both are already dependencies of this package. Do not change the file's 2022 copyright year.

behaviour: Proves the hook redirects a stale ref to the renamed entity preserving the sub-path, query and fragment, issues no extra request on the happy path, and leaves an unknown ref alone.
rules: 1. Render the hook with `renderHook` from '@testing-library/react' inside a wrapper that supplies `catalogApiRef` via TestApiProvider, and mock `react-router-dom`'s `useNavigate` and `useRouteRef` the way the sibling useExternalRedirect.test.tsx does, so the navigate target is directly assertable.
2. At most four thorough `it` blocks.

3. Block one, the happy path costs nothing (FR-16, NFR-1): when getEntityByRef returns an entity, assert the hook returns it, assert `queryEntities` was NEVER called, and assert navigate was never called. This is the guard that an ordinary lookup issues no additional request.

4. Block two, the redirect and sub-path preservation (FR-12, AC-19): getEntityByRef returns undefined and queryEntities returns exactly one renamed entity. Assert navigate was called once, with `{ replace: true }`, with a state object carrying the canonicalized former ref, and with a target that carries the NEW ref AND the original sub-path, search string and fragment. Drive this from an initial route of the form `/catalog/default/component/old-name/docs?tab=x#frag` so all three carried parts are exercised in one assertion set.

5. Block three, unknown ref ends on not-found (FR-15, AC-9): getEntityByRef returns undefined and queryEntities returns zero items. Assert navigate was never called, the hook's returned entity is undefined, and loading settles to false — so the caller renders the existing not-found UI.

6. Block four, one attempt per ref: with getEntityByRef returning undefined and queryEntities returning zero items, re-render the hook several times for the same ref and assert queryEntities was called exactly once, proving the useRef guard holds across remounts.

7. Bind the route ref through renderHook's wrapper using `mountedRoutes` with entityRouteRef, so the route function the hook calls resolves real paths rather than a stub, per the repo's route-ref convention.
8. Do not add a test id to the implementation. Apache 2.0 header with year 2026.
